Andrew the First-Called

Icons

Saints

St. Andrew the First-Called

St. Andrew the First-Called Apostle

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

John 1:40–42

King James Version · Scripture previews

St. Andrew the First-Called is identified in the Greek church reading as Peter’s brother from Bethsaida and a former disciple of St. John the Baptist. His icon is therefore distinct from those of St. Andrew of Crete or other saints named Andrew.

[1] November 30, Reading, identity and calling

What is depicted

The displayed historical icon comes from Saint Paraskevi’s church at Langadas. Its catalogue identifies the Apostle Andrew and dates it before the twentieth century. He is shown as an aged apostle holding a scroll; the file’s named subject distinguishes him from homonymous saints.

[2] Exact artwork file: Description, Creator, Date, Credit and licence fields; complete downloaded image visually compared

History and tradition

GOARCH explains the title First-Called through Andrew’s response to St. John the Baptist’s witness and his following of Christ. It later recounts missionary work and crucifixion at Patras, associating the X-shaped cross with his memory. The martyrdom detail is a church tradition beyond the Gospel reading below.

[1] November 30, Reading, apostolic mission and traditional martyrdom

Published explanation

One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.

And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.

[3] John 1:40–42
